value.body: An aero-engine technician works on aircraft engines, servicing them on the aircraft during line and base checks or stripping and rebuilding them in an engine shop. MRO organisations, airline engineering departments and engine overhaul shops hire for this work. A typical shift involves inspections, part changes, tests and careful paperwork for each task.

items.label: Aircraft with Indian scheduled airlines
items.note: Aircraft endorsed on airline operator certificates; ~110 were inducted during 2023. Aircraft actually flying can be fewer
items.source: MoCA reply in Rajya Sabha (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually join an MRO or airline as a trainee technician after an AME course. Engine-type training and DGCA licence modules are built up over the first years under supervision.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Gas turbine and piston engine basics

value.title: At a glance
items: Common next roles: licensed engineer (B1), engine shop inspector, powerplant specialist.
Engine work demands strict procedure-following; errors are costly.
Shift work in hangars and shops is standard.
